text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR. It catches fresh issues before they merge, which reduces rework and improves quality without slowing teams down. The trade-off is delayed feedback for the PR author—they won’t see the review until after submission—but the net gain in stability justifies it.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks exposing *new* edge cases that could destabilize the PR’s core logic before the author can address them, turning a quality tool into a liability. A better alternative is running PR-Agent on the oldest merged PR first—it tests stale routing/prompts without threatening active work, and the feedback loop is already closed. Settle this by measuring the false-positive rate in shadow mode versus the oldest PR; if shadow mode flags more critical issues, adopt it—but only after validating the model’s routing/prompts aren’t the problem.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first to validate its routing and prompts without risking active work, then expand to the newest open PR once stability is confirmed. This reduces the chance of destabilizing fresh changes while still catching issues early in the pipeline.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first. It validates routing and prompts against real but stale changes, proving stability before touching active work. The trade-off is delayed detection of issues in fresh PRs, but that risk is acceptable because fresh PRs are already under human review. Once the oldest PR confirms PR-Agent’s safety, expand to the newest open PR. This sequence minimizes disruption while ensuring the tool works before it impacts live work.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first to validate routing/prompts, then expand to the newest open PR once stability is confirmed.

Result: A proven stable PR-Agent setup that catches issues without disrupting active work, owned by Overhaul.
